title: What can the other number be if m is one of them?
description: In a pair whose highest common factor is one of the two numbers, the other number can be a multiple or a factor of m. The same is shown for seven k, with fourteen k and seven as examples. Keeko doubts this and thinks the other number can only be a multiple of m.
teaching_notes: One idea: in such a pair the other number is either a multiple or a factor of the given number. Watch for students who list only multiples and forget the factors.

source: If m is one of the numbers in such a pair, what could the other number be? Do the same when 7k is one of the numbers.
video_script.why: The child has seen that the highest common factor is one of the numbers when one number is a factor of the other and now writes that with letters.
video_script.substitution: The two numbers can sit either way round, so the other number is a multiple or a factor of the given one.
video_script.anchor: The letter m written in a box, with an empty box beside it for the other number.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks the other number can only be a multiple of m, but a factor of m works too, because then m is the multiple and the factor is the highest common factor.
video_script.payoff_line: The other number is a multiple or a factor

final_answer.value: (a) any multiple or factor of m (b) any multiple or factor of 7k, such as 14k or 7
final_answer.spoken: any multiple or factor of m

hold_back: any multiple or factor of m
never_show: only multiples of m, marked right
maths_rules: if the other number is a multiple of m, such as 2m, 3m or 10m, then m goes into it and the HCF is m
if the other number is a factor of m, then it goes into m and the HCF is that factor, one of the two numbers
for 7k: multiples such as 14k and 21k; factors such as 7 and k
6 and 18 can be read either way round: with m = 6 the other is the multiple 18; with m = 18 the other is the factor 6
video_script.design: One idea: the two numbers can sit either way round, so the partner is a multiple or a factor. The box for m stays on the board through all the steps.
